extracted.intended_audience: eRA Commons users (PD/PIs, PI delegates, Signing Officials (SOs), AOs) who prepare, check, route, and submit RPPRs and PRAMs and use the Status module
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and quality requirements for preparing, validating, routing, and submitting Research Performance Progress Reports (RPPRs) and Progress Report Additional Materials (PRAMs) and for using the eRA Commons Status module. Covers error checking, file requirements, role-based permissions, routing/recall/submit workflows, and search/actions in Status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiscal-year IER data locked after award
rubrics_metrics.description: After a grant is awarded, only the View links will be available for the IERs associated with fiscal year award. The data for a given fiscal year is locked when the award is issued and no further updates can be made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: At that point, updates must be made via Status for the record associated with the next fiscal year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform error check before RPPR submission
rubrics_metrics.description: At any time before an RPPR is submitted to agency, an error check can be performed to verify that the report passes the business rules and system validations in place. Any user who has access to the RPPR may perform the error check.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Errors and warnings are underlined and linked; click the error description to be taken to the screen and field where the error was found.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two methods to check for errors
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two ways to check for errors: (1) Check for errors on the current form using the Check for Errors button at the bottom of the current form; (2) Check for errors on all forms at once using the Check for Errors option in the three-dot ellipsis menu on the RPPR Menu screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To check only a single form (e.g., Section B. Accomplishments) go to that form and click the Check for Errors button at the bottom of the form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Errors must be corrected prior to submission; warnings do not block submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Listed errors, which are clickable, must be corrected prior to submission; the system will prevent submission of an RPPR containing errors. However, the system will not prevent submission of an RPPR when a warning message is displayed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all validations pass, a message displays indicating: No errors found on validation. Warnings are in yellow; errors are in red/pink.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF uploads should be flattened
rubrics_metrics.description: All PDFs you upload are recommended to be a flattened PDF, and may cause an error if not flattened.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the FAQ titled, 'When submitting PDFs to eRA Commons, particularly for RPPRs and Just-in-Time, I am getting an error telling me to ensure all files are flattened PDFs. What does flattening a PDF mean and how do you do it?' for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-project RPPR error-check workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: For single-project RPPRs you can check for errors on the entire RPPR using the Check for Errors menu option under the three-dot ellipsis menu on the RPPR Menu screen, or check only a single form using the Check for Errors button on that form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If errors or a warning exist, the appropriate message displays; errors must be corrected prior to submission while warnings do not block submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multi-project RPPR error-check workflow
rubrics_metrics.description: For multi-project RPPRs you can check for errors on the entire RPPR using the Check for Errors menu option under the three-dot ellipsis menu on the RPPR Menu screen, or check the Overall or individual component by selecting Check for Errors for the Overall or component being validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If errors or warnings exist for the chosen component, the appropriate messages display and listed errors must be corrected prior to submission. Agency-specific exception: Department of Commerce (DOC) topic does not apply to DOC award RPPRs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing RPPR as PDF from Status
rubrics_metrics.description: The RPPR, in PDF format, is accessible in Commons within the Status Information screen. Use the Status module -> List of Applications/Grants -> select the Application ID -> Other Relevant Documents to view the RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For incrementally-funded RPPR: click the e-Application link. For multi-year funded awards: click the appropriate year's link (appears as RPPR Year <X> <MM/DD/YYYY>). The PDF opens in a separate window. The submitted RPPR can also be accessed from the RPPR Menu screen via the View RPPR As PDF option under the three-dot ellipsis icon.

rubrics_metrics.name: PD/PI Assurance Report access and search
rubrics_metrics.description: The PD/PI Assurance Report displays instances when PI users agreed to the PD/PI Assurance message upon routing or submitting RPPRs. SO role has access to the PD/PI Assurance Report menu option; principal investigators (PI) cannot see this screen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You can perform a search for a specific PI, by a range of dates for all PIs in the organization, or by using both criteria. A search with no specified PI returns the records for all PIs in the organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and handling of Public Access PRAM
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Access PRAM lets awardees upload, review, and submit information in response to automated notification sent when an NIH awardee submits an RPPR with non-compliant publications. The automated email requests verification that all publications are in compliance with the NIH Public Access Policy; SO and AO assigned to the RPPR receive a copy (cc).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the PRAM screen, awardees can upload a My NCBI PDF report demonstrating previously non-compliant papers are now compliant. Compliant papers have status of Complete, N/A, PMC Journal in Process, or In process at NIHMS. If unable to provide verification, awardees can upload justification for why publications cannot be brought into compliance. Public Access PRAM can be submitted only one time, and only one file can be submitted. Agency-specific: not applicable for DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: PRAM role-based submission authority
rubrics_metrics.description: As with the RPPR, a PD/PI (or Contact PI for multiple PIs) can enter the PRAM, but can only submit it if the PD/PI is delegated with Submit Progress Report authority. Otherwise, only the SO can submit the PRAM to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Route button is missing, the request might be in another user's queue. Only the current reviewer can edit the PRAM; PIs do not see a Submit button (SO only).

rubrics_metrics.name: PRAM upload file restrictions and actions
rubrics_metrics.description: The PRAM screen includes a 'Drop Files Here...' area that specifies how many files and what file types are allowed. For uploaded files, users can Download or Delete via icons; only the current reviewer can delete the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After adding files, available actions include Preview (see entire PRAM submission package summary and contents), View Routing History, Route, Recall, and Submit (SO only).

rubrics_metrics.name: Routing PRAM to next reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: To route a PRAM click the Route button, select a name from the Next Reviewer dropdown, optionally enter Comments, and click Submit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are a PI the Route PRAM to Next Reviewer screen displays the PD/PI Assurance statement which PIs should read and confirm; SOs do not see this screen. Routing triggers a notification email to the person to whom the request is routed and updates status to Reviewer Work in Progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of routing: Reviewer Work In Progress and editing limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: After routing, the status is updated and shown as Reviewer Work in Progress. At this point, the PD/PI can only view the PRAM, the attachments, the Preview, and the Routing History; the PD/PI cannot edit the PRAM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SO can route the PRAM back to the contact PI, or the PI can click the Recall button to reassign the PRAM back to the PI (subject to recall rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recalling a PRAM
rubrics_metrics.description: A PRAM in status Reviewer Work in Progress that has been routed can be recalled by the contact PI or any SO at the organization up until the submission of the current PRAM attachment(s) to the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recalling is useful if routed to the wrong person or reviewer unavailable. A PD/PI delegate does not have the ability to recall the PRAM. After a recall, the person to whom the request had been assigned receives a notification email that they are no longer the current reviewer. Prior PRAM submissions to the Agency are not included in the recall.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submitting the PRAM (SO-only unless PD/PI delegated)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the PRAM is in Reviewer Work in Progress status, the current reviewer can submit it to the agency. Any signing official can submit. The PD/PI can submit only if delegated Submit Progress Report authority by an SO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To submit a PRAM, use the Status module to search for an award, select Agency Requested PRAM (or Public Access PRAM) from the three-dot ellipsis menu or Action column, click the Submit button, read the certification statement and click the I Agree button.

rubrics_metrics.name: Viewing submitted PRAMs in Status Information
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting a PRAM, users can view the PRAM via the Status Information screen by looking up an award and clicking the PRAM link under Other Relevant Documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PRAM file opens as a PDF with a header for each PRAM submission followed by the uploaded documents. If multiple submissions were completed, submissions are separated with the most recent displayed first followed by earlier submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency-Requested PRAM differences
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency Requested PRAM lets the awardee attach, review, route, and submit information in response to a specific request by the program official (PO) at the awarding IC or agency for additional information following the submission of an RPPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with RPPR/PRAM rules, PD/PI can enter but only SO or delegated PD/PI can submit. Agency-requested PRAM can be submitted multiple times as long as the Agency Requested PRAM link remains available in the Status module. Note: Agency Requested PRAM is not available for multi-year funded awards; Public Access PRAM is not applicable for DOC awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status module role-based visibility and capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: What you can see and do in the Status module depends on the role associated with your Commons account (PD/PIs, their delegates, and SOs have different views and permissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Status lets users track application status, view applications and NoAs and other documents, complete post-submission and post-award transactions, access and update Human Subjects information through HSS, and (SOs only) bypass the 2-business-day viewing window for administrative supplements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessing the Status module
rubrics_metrics.description: To access the Status module after logging into eRA Commons, either click the Status button on the main eRA Commons home page or select Status from the main menu under the eRA logo.

rubrics_metrics.name: General search: use either award number fields OR Project Number (not both)
rubrics_metrics.description: With the general search you can search on the various parts of the award number (type, activity code, IC, serial number, support year, suffix) or you can search by Project Number for contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NOTE: Use either the six award number fields OR use the Project Number field; do not use both simultaneously because each searches a different type of numbering system and no results will appear when they are used together.

rubrics_metrics.name: Status Search types and specialized searches
rubrics_metrics.description: Status supports multiple search types (General, Just in Time, Recently Awarded, Closeout, Relinquishing Statements, Recent/Pending eSubmissions, Re-Assign Award, ESI Eligibility, Search in ASSIST etc.) each designed for specific workflows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some searches redirect to other modules (e.g., ASSIST). See the referenced help pages for details on each search type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpreting Status search results columns
rubrics_metrics.description: Status Result displays columns such as Application/Award ID (link to Status Information), Grants.gov Tracking #, Proposal Title, PD/PI Name, Application Status, Project Period and Budget Dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If multiple PIs exist an MPI indicator appears next to the application ID. 'NFP (no further processing)' may be added to Proposal Title to indicate the application will not be referred for review. For a list of each application status see the era status codes document.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-dot ellipsis possible actions on awards
rubrics_metrics.description: Various actions can appear in the three-dot ellipsis menu for an award (Accept/Decline Award; Administrative Supplement; Agency Requested PRAM; Closed; Correspondence; Extension; Human Subjects; JIT; Public Access PRAM; Reject eApplication; Requires Closeout; Revision Request; RPPR; Start Relinquishing Statement; Transmittal Sheet; Show Prior Errors and Warnings; View Prior eSubmissions; View Terms Tracking).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some actions are role- or agency-specific (e.g., Accept/Decline Award and Revision Request are DOC only; Reject eApplication is available only to SOs). Use the appropriate action to access the respective feature (e.g., JIT opens the Just In Time screen).

rubrics_metrics.name: Two-business-day application viewing window for SO/AOR
rubrics_metrics.description: After submitting an application, there is a two-business-day application viewing window for SOs/AORs to check the application and reject and revise it. The application automatically moves forward to agency staff after the viewing window elapses unless explicitly rejected in eRA Commons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For administrative supplements this two-day viewing window can be skipped; see bypassing documentation for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Searching Recent/Pending eSubmissions criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: For Recent/Pending eSubmissions searches use criteria such as Grants.gov Tracking #, Accession Number, eSubmission Status (All, Pending Verification, or Rejected), and Received Date Range.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the search results, actions such as showing prior errors appear in the three-dot ellipsis menu next to the Award/Application ID.

rubrics_metrics.name: eSubmission tracking: handle 'eSubmission Error' results
rubrics_metrics.description: If the eSubmission Status column shows 'eSubmission Error', check prior errors and warnings and open the Application ID to view submission errors/warnings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select Show Prior Errors and Warnings from the three-dot ellipsis menu, then click the linked Application ID to open Status Information where existing submission errors or warnings display in yellow or pink box.
